description_full: ITT Inc., together with its subsidiaries, manufactures and sells engineered critical components and customized technology solutions for the transportation, industrial, and energy markets. The company operates three segments: Motion Technologies, Industrial Process, and Connect & Control Technologies. The Motion Technologies segment manufactures brake pads, shock absorbers, energy absorption components, and damping technologies primarily for the transportation industry, including passenger cars, trucks, light and heavy-duty commercial and military vehicles, buses, and trains. This segment sells its products under the ITT Friction Technologies, KONI, Axtone, and Novitek brand names. The Industrial Process segment provides industrial pumps, valves, plant optimization, and remote monitoring systems and services; and aftermarket solutions, such as replacement parts and services. It serves various customers in the energy, chemical and petrochemical, pharmaceutical, general industrial, marine, mining, pulp and paper, food and beverage, power generation, and biopharmaceutical industries. This segment sells its products under the Goulds Pumps, Bornemann, Engineered Valves, Hamworthy Pumps, PRO Services, C'treat, Svanehøj, Rheinhütte Pumpen, and Habonim brand names. The Connect & Control Technologies segment offers engineered connectors, cable assemblies, and specialized products for critical applications supporting various markets, including aerospace and defence, industrial, transportation, medical, and energy under the Cannon, VEAM, BIW Connector Systems, CIA&D, Compulink, Aerospace Controls, Enidine, Compact Automation, Charles E. Gillman, Turn-Act, Neo-Dyn, TopFlite Components, Conoflow, VIDAR, kSARIA, and Micro-Mode brand names. It operates in North America, Europe, Asia, the Middle East, Africa, and South America. The company was incorporated in 1920 and is headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut.

financial_summary: ITT Inc. is a large-cap industrials business with a $19.7B market cap on $3.9B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +10% over the past three years and +5% annually across the full decade, a respectable pace for a business of this size.
Returns on capital run at 19% against a 10% cost of capital — a 9-point spread that is the clearest signature of an economic moat, with gross margins sitting at 32%.

The business throws off $548M in free cash flow — roughly 14 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 1.37× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 14× is fortress-like.

Net dilution runs at 3.5% annually, transferring value from owners to stock-based comp, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and within its sector the business captures 1.6× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.

sect: Its 17% operating margin runs 8pp above the Industrials median (9%), a real cost or pricing edge over peers.
It captures 1.56x its revenue share in sector profits, taking a disproportionate slice of the profit pool.
Over five years it has been gaining share of the sector profit pool (+11.1% a year).
The sector is fragmented and competitive (HHI 0.01 across 550 companies in the universe; the top four hold 9% of revenue), so pricing power is hard to come by.
mkt: The shares have drifted higher, up 6% over the past year excluding the latest month.
The price sits near the top of its 52-week range, 4% below the high.
With annualised volatility of 33% and a beta of 1.22, it amplifies market moves.
Liquidity is deep, with about $160.6M traded a day.
In past sell-offs it fell 50% in the 2020 crash, 38% in the 2022 bear market and 52% in 2008.
val: The price sits above its DCF fair value of $133 (margin of safety -66%), so there is no valuation cushion.
The fair-value models disagree (dispersion 39%), and the Monte Carlo range runs $64.67 to $312 (P10-P90), so treat the estimate as noisy.
On multiples it looks expensive against Industrials peers: P/E 45.4 vs 23.1, EV/EBITDA 20.7 vs 13.3 and P/FCF 35.9 vs 22.4 (sector median).
Against its own history it is dear: the EBIT multiple sits 79% above its 10-year median.
Earnings yields are thin: an FCF yield of 2.8% (below the risk-free rate) and an EBIT/EV of 3.0% (vs the 8% bar).
The 13 covering analysts target $256 on average, 16% above the price, well away from the model's fair value.
prof: ROIC of 19% clears the cost of capital of 10.3% by 9pp, the mark of a value creator; returns have swung a lot from year to year (CV 1.18).
It runs a 32% gross margin and converts 14% of revenue into free cash flow.
Earnings quality looks solid: cash conversion of 1.37x.
ROE of 12% comes mostly from margins and asset turnover rather than leverage (1.5x equity multiplier).
It spends 2.8% of revenue on R&D and 0.9% on stock compensation.
hlth: The balance sheet carries net cash of $960.1M (5% of market cap).
No distress or manipulation flags (Altman Z 7.4, in the safe zone).
growth: Revenue has compounded at 9.6% over 3 years, 9.7% over 5 years and 4.7% over 10 years, and it has been lumpy (year-to-year swings of 22%).
At current returns, reinvesting 100% of profits supports about 19.3% a year of fundamental growth, enough to sustain growth.
Free cash flow has compounded 8.0% a year over five years.
Forward indicators: a book-to-bill of 1.07 (orders outpacing sales), a backlog worth 48% of annual revenue and deferred revenue up 46%.
Capex roughly matches depreciation (0.8x, 3.1% of sales), a maintenance pace.
Its Rule of 40 score is 23, below the 40 that marks a healthy growth business.
own: Insiders hold little stock (0.5%), and reported institutional holdings exceed 100% of shares (a sign of heavy share lending).
Insider trading is two-way: 2 purchases and 8 sales over the past year, net $279K sold.
Net share issuance leaves shareholder yield negative (-3.5%), diluting holders.
The share count has grown 0.9% a year over five years, diluting existing holders.
It has paid a dividend for 30 consecutive years, raising it 13.5% a year over the last five.
people: With about 11,600 employees, each generates about $340K of revenue, in line with the Industrials median, and revenue has fallen 6.2% a year across its filed history.
That works out to $47K of free cash flow per employee.
CEO pay is $4.0M (12x revenue per employee), and compensation governance scores well (2/10, lower is better).
